headline: Plan for Seasonal Float Permits and Sandhills Stays
reservation: River access is managed by both the National Park Service and private outfitters; confirm your launch window and equipment rental in advance, especially for July weekends. Camping at Smith Falls State Park or local ranch-based glamping sites requires early booking through the Nebraska Game and Parks system. Official checks on river water levels and seasonal flow are recommended prior to departure.

days.title: Canyons and River Rhythms

stops.name: Cornell Bridge
stops.detail: Start your float here for a classic introduction to the sandstone canyon and calm water.

stops.name: Smith Falls State Park
stops.detail: Take a break from the water to see Nebraska's highest waterfall via the footbridge.

days.driving: Allow 30–60 minutes for outfitter shuttles; river time is roughly 4–6 hours depending on pace.
days.note: River currents are generally slow but check for seasonal debris or submerged logs.

days.title: Prairie Wildlife and Sandhills Scenery
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Refuge Entrance

stops.name: Fort Niobrara National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Drive the wildlife loop to view bison and elk in their natural prairie habitat.

stops.name: The Cowboy Trail
stops.detail: Walk or bike the segment crossing the Niobrara River bridge for panoramic valley views.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the refuge loop; conditions are gravel-based.
days.note: Stay inside your vehicle at the refuge; bison are wild animals and can be unpredictable.

days.title: Hidden Springs and Lower River Reach

stops.name: Big Springs
stops.detail: Observe the unique ecological 'crossroads' where groundwater seeps from the canyon walls.

stops.name: Rocky Ford
stops.detail: Visit this area for the unique limestone ledge scenery, often used as a take-out point for longer floats.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for travel to lower river access points; roads may be narrow.
days.note: Portaging may be required at specific low-head areas; follow outfitter guidance.

intel.title: Landing Access
intel.text: Parking at popular landings like Smith Falls can be congested during peak summer Saturdays. Utilize outfitter shuttle services to avoid leaving vehicles at remote river access points.

intel.title: Sandhills Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is extremely limited or non-existent within the river canyon. Download offline maps and notify others of your float plan before leaving the town of Valentine.

intel.title: Valentine Supply Hub
intel.text: Valentine is the primary location for fuel and groceries in the region. Ensure your tank is full before heading to remote refuge entrances or western canyon access points.

intel.title: Float Duration
intel.text: Allow ample time for your float; a 'two-hour' trip can easily double if you stop for swimming or birdwatching. Most outfitters require equipment returns by late afternoon.

intel.title: Seasonal Flow
intel.text: The river is spring-fed and remains floatable most of the year, but spring run-off can increase speed. Check with the NPS Visitor Center for current river hazards.

plan.arrival: Fly into Sioux Gateway (SUX) or North Platte; drive to Valentine to stock up on river gear, snacks, and water before heading to your riverside camp.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is beneficial for gravel refuge roads; check rental agreements for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Niobrara Valley Overlook provides a wide view of the canyon catching the low sun, particularly vivid in autumn.
